newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pick 'n Pay sees year pre-tax up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pick 'n Pay sees year pre-tax up 20 pct.

text.p: Pick 'n Pay Stores Ltd chairman Raymond Ackerman on Tuesday predicted 20 percent pre-tax profit growth in the year to February 28, 1997.

"With these results under our belts, we confidently expect a year-end result of 20 percent pre-tax profit increase and a larger figure for headline earnings per share," Ackerman said after unveiling a jump in half-year profits.

Announcing earnings per share growth of 10.37 cents and an interim dividend of 3.8 cents for the six months to August 31, against 8.25 and 2.92 a year ago, Ackerman said 13 new stores would open in the second half and eight would be renovated.
The company said it was expected to make a major announcement in the convenience store market later this year, with the launch of a new brand SA Cafe.
"The company is also in negotiation with 7-Eleven to broaden its successful Western Cape operations countrywide," a statement said.
This deal was subject to the outcome of a court interdict due to be heard on November 25.
Ackerman said that it was clear that the work done over the last three to four years to re-position the group was now bearing fruit.
He said crime remained a dominant factor which was affecting morale, not only of customers, but also of staff.
